title: Two AI launches on the same day
content: On 7 October 2026 Anthropic released Claude Haiku 5.5 and OpenAI began rolling GPT-6 out across every ChatGPT tier.

title: Anthropic went cheap
content: Anthropic called Haiku 5.5 "the cheapest, fastest, and most capable small model we've ever released".

title: About 75% cheaper on average
content: Anthropic says Haiku 5.5 costs about 75% less than Haiku 4.5 on average: 90% less for requests up to 100,000 tokens and 50% less above that.

title: OpenAI went visual
content: OpenAI launched Intelligent UI, which puts interactive buttons, calculators, charts and editable graphs inside ChatGPT answers, TechCrunch reported.

title: GPT-6 for paying users first
content: GPT-6 with Intelligent UI rolled out globally to Pro, Plus, Business and Enterprise users on Wednesday 7 October.

title: Free users the next day
content: ChatGPT's free and lower-cost Go tiers get GPT-6 and Intelligent UI on Thursday 8 October, according to TechCrunch.

title: The story in one line
content: Capable AI is getting much cheaper for developers and far more widely available to consumers, both on the same day.

title: Input: $0.10 per million tokens
content: For requests up to 100,000 tokens, Haiku 5.5 input costs $0.10 per million tokens, against $1.00 for Haiku 4.5.

title: Output: $0.50 per million tokens
content: Output costs $0.50 per million tokens up to 100,000 tokens, against $5.00 for Haiku 4.5.

title: Long requests cost more
content: Above 100,000 tokens, Haiku 5.5 costs $0.50 per million input tokens and $2.50 per million output tokens.

title: Cache reads at a cent
content: Cache reads cost $0.01 per million tokens for shorter requests and $0.05 above 100,000 tokens.

title: Compared with Sonnet 5.5
content: Sonnet 5.5 costs $2.00 per million input tokens and $10.00 per million output tokens, so Haiku 5.5 is a fraction of the price for short requests.

title: Sonnet got cheaper too
content: Anthropic cut Sonnet 5.5 cache reads by 50%, from $0.20 to $0.10 per million tokens, which it says lowers most agentic task costs by about 20%.

title: A catch: more tokens per task
content: Haiku 5.5 uses the same updated tokenizer as Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5, so Anthropic says it uses slightly more tokens per task.

title: Built for volume
content: Anthropic aims Haiku 5.5 at high-volume, cost-sensitive work such as summarisation, compaction, database queries and classification.

title: A subagent for bigger models
content: Anthropic positions Haiku 5.5 as a subagent working alongside Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 on coding tasks.

title: Also for support and browsing
content: Anthropic says Haiku 5.5 suits live customer support and browser use.

title: The fastest at standard speed
content: Haiku 5.5 is Anthropic's fastest model at standard speed, though Opus models in Fast Mode are quicker.

title: First Haiku with an effort dial
content: Haiku 5.5 is the first Haiku-class model with adjustable effort, from Low through Med, High and Xhigh to Max.

title: Trade cost for intelligence
content: The effort setting lets developers choose how much reasoning, and therefore cost, each request gets.

title: Model ID
content: Developers call it as claude-haiku-5-5.

title: Available everywhere
content: Haiku 5.5 is available on the Claude Platform, Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud and Microsoft Azure.

title: Office work: 1620 vs 735
content: On GDPval-AA v2.1, Haiku 5.5 scored 1620, against 735 for Haiku 4.5 and 1840 for Sonnet 5.5.

title: Beating GPT-6 Luna on office tasks
content: Anthropic's table puts GPT-6 Luna at 1437 on GDPval-AA v2.1, below Haiku 5.5's 1620.

title: Computer use: 72.4%
content: On an offline subset of OSWorld 2.1, Haiku 5.5 scored 72.4%, up from 15.7% for Haiku 4.5. Anthropic lists GPT-6 Luna at 48.9%.

title: Humanity's Last Exam: 45.9%
content: Without tools, Haiku 5.5 scored 45.9% on Humanity's Last Exam, against 10.2% for Haiku 4.5. With tools it scored 57.4%.

title: Terminal-Bench 4.0: 39.2%
content: Haiku 5.5 scored 39.2% on Terminal-Bench 4.0, against 0.0% for Haiku 4.5 and 70.6% for Sonnet 5.5.

title: Coding: 46.4% on FrontierCode
content: Haiku 5.5 scored 46.4% on FrontierCode 1.1 Main, against 42.4% for GPT-6 Luna in Anthropic's table.

title: Charts: 46.4% without tools
content: On Chartography without tools, Haiku 5.5 scored 46.4%, against 6.4% for Haiku 4.5.

title: Still not a Sonnet
content: Anthropic says Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5 remain better for complex agentic coding.

title: Vendor numbers
content: These are Anthropic's own reported results. Independent tests may differ.

title: Asana: over 30% lower latency
content: Asana reported over 30% lower latency on task completions and up to 2.5 times faster inference per agent turn.

title: HubSpot: 92.8% on CRM tests
content: HubSpot reported a 92.8% average over three runs on its CRM evaluation suite, the best it had seen from a smaller model.

title: AlphaSense: 0.84 vs 0.76
content: AlphaSense scored Haiku 5.5 at 0.84 against 0.76 for Haiku 4.5 across 400 queries.

title: Box: 11 points higher
content: Box said Haiku 5.5 scored 11 points higher than Haiku 4.5 at about half the latency.

title: Rogo: quick lookups
content: Rogo uses it as a subagent for jobs such as pulling segment revenue from a 10-K filing.

title: Cognition: a sidekick in Devin
content: Cognition added Haiku 5.5 as a sidekick in Devin Fusion, alongside Opus 5.5 as lead, to cut cost and latency.

title: Fewer misaligned behaviours
content: Anthropic reports major alignment improvements over Haiku 4.5, including less willingness to cooperate with misuse.

title: Cyber safeguards in the middle
content: Haiku 5.5's cyber safeguards are stricter than Haiku 4.5's but looser than Sonnet 5.5's. It allows more defensive work but blocks penetration testing.

title: Biology rules match Sonnet
content: Haiku 5.5 uses the same biology safeguards as Sonnet 5, Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.

title: Verification still applies
content: Organisations needing more can apply to Anthropic's Life Sciences and Cyber Verification Programs.

title: ChatGPT stops being just text
content: OpenAI product manager Aarush Selvan said ChatGPT "has predominantly been a text-based interface".

title: Better answers aren't just words
content: Selvan said the most helpful answers "aren't just text".

title: The aeroplane wing demo
content: In a demo, Selvan asked ChatGPT how an aeroplane wing generates lift, and it answered with several diagrams.

title: Recipes, bikes and hikes
content: OpenAI's examples included recipe visuals, a bicycle mechanics diagram, a multi-day hiking map and a personal savings calculator.

title: You can turn it down
content: Users can reduce the number of visuals in answers, like other ChatGPT personality settings.

title: Aimed at learning
content: OpenAI says the goal is to make "learning complex topics easier".

title: GPT-6's long road
content: Bloomberg reported on 3 September that GPT-6 Astra first went to approved business testers, with a guardrailed version planned for paid ChatGPT users.

title: API credits for subscribers
content: Anthropic now gives Max 5x subscribers $100 a month in API credits, Max 20x subscribers $200 and Team plans up to $500, pooled across users.

title: SDKs gain computer use
content: Anthropic's Python and TypeScript SDKs now support computer use and browser use in beta.

title: Small models do big jobs
content: Haiku 5.5's scores show a small, cheap model now handling office and computer-use tasks that older small models failed.

title: Agents get cheaper to run
content: Multi-agent systems spend most tokens on routine subtasks, so a cheaper subagent cuts the cost of the whole system.

title: The consumer front moves to interface
content: OpenAI's bet is that how answers look and behave matters as much as the model behind them.

title: Benchmarks name rivals
content: Anthropic's launch table compares directly with GPT-6 Luna, a sign of how closely the labs now track each other.

title: Independent benchmarks
content: Watch for third-party tests of Haiku 5.5 and GPT-6.

title: OpenAI's price response
content: Watch whether OpenAI cuts prices on its small models in response.

title: Free-tier reception
content: Watch how ChatGPT's free users take to Intelligent UI after the rollout.

title: Snapshot date
content: This pack reflects sources opened on 8 October 2026. Later evidence should go in a new dated pack.
